That is like a seesaw or a doorknob: when you push one side of the axis, the other side moves. Just a small push near the axis makes the head end move a lot. Another guess is that they hang on an axis and swing. That is like a swing or a mobile.

strings.浮く力: 水が押し返す力。紙の器は中に空気があるので浮く。濡れると紙が重くなって: Floating force: The force of the water pushing back. A paper container floats because it has air inside. When it gets wet, the paper becomes heavy and sinks easily.

strings.浮く力: 水に浮く物は、押しのけた水の重さだけ上へ押される。空洞があると軽くなっ: Floating force: A thing that floats on water is pushed up by a force as big as the weight of the water it pushes aside. If it has a hollow inside, it is lighter and floats more easily.
strings.浮く力: 水に浮く物は、押しのけた水の重さだけ上へ押される。紙は水を吸うと重くな: Floating force: A thing that floats on water is pushed up by a force as big as the weight of the water it pushes aside. Paper gets heavy when it soaks up water, so protect it with wax or oil.

strings.独楽が倒れずに回るのは、自転車の車輪が回っている間は倒れにくいのと同じです。重さ: A top spins without falling for the same reason a bicycle wheel is hard to knock over while it is turning. If the weight is spread evenly around the core, the core spins without wobbling. The guess that you twist the knob uses the same finger movement as turning a plastic bottle cap, and the guess that you wind a cord and pull it is like pulling thread off a spool.

strings.独楽は、回っている間は倒れずに立ちます。自転車の車輪が回っている間は倒れにくいの: A spinning top stays up and does not fall while it is spinning. It is like a bicycle wheel, which is hard to tip over while it spins: the spin tries to keep it pointing the same way. The guess that you twist it with your fingers is like turning the cap of a plastic bottle. If you make the core thin and long, you can spin it more times in your hand.

strings.足を開く: 両足の間を広げると支える面が広がる。揺れる電車で足を開いて立つのと同: Opening the feet: If you widen the space between the feet, the supporting surface gets wider. It is the same as standing with your feet apart on a shaking train.
strings.車の付いた台を糸で引く仮説は、引き車や、紐で引く木のおもちゃと同じです。車が台の: The guess that a stand with wheels is pulled by a string works like a pull cart, or a wooden toy you pull with a cord. When the wheels turn in the holes of the stand, the stand rolls along without scraping the floor. The guess that it sits on a slope is like letting a toy car run down a slope: its weight pushes it downhill.
strings.車の大きさ: 車の半径が、軸から台の縁までより小さいと、台が床に触れてこすれる: Wheel size: If the wheel’s radius is smaller than the distance from the axle to the edge of the stand, the stand touches the floor and drags.
strings.転がり: 丸い物は床とこすれる所が点か線だけなので、滑るより小さな力で動く: Rolling: A round thing touches the floor only at a point or along a line, so it takes less force to move than sliding.
strings.転がり: 車が回ると、床とこすれる力がとても小さくなる。引きずるより軽く動くわけ: Rolling: When a wheel turns, the rubbing against the floor becomes very small. That is why it moves more easily than when it is dragged.
strings.転がり: 車が軸の周りで回ると、床をこすらずに進める。引きずるより小さな力で動く: Rolling: When a wheel turns around its axle, it moves without rubbing the floor. It moves with less force than dragging.
strings.軸: 真ん中に軸を通して引くと、俵は軸の周りで回りながら進む（糸巻きと同じ）: Axle: If you put an axle through the middle and pull, the bale turns around the axle as it moves (the same as a spool).
strings.軸と前の壁の間（mm）: Gap between the axle and the front wall (mm)
strings.軸の摩擦: 軸が穴でこすれると回りにくい。穴を少し大きくするか、ビーズを挟む: Friction at the axle: If the axle rubs in the hole, it is hard to turn. Make the hole a little bigger, or put a bead in between.
strings.軸の摩擦: 軸が穴の中でこすれると回りにくい。穴を少し大きくするか、軸を滑らかに: Friction at the axle: If the axle rubs in the hole, it is hard to turn. Make the hole a little bigger, or make the axle smooth.
strings.軽さ: 軽い置物は押されて動きやすいが、倒れても壊れにくい: Lightness: A light ornament is easy to push around, but it does not break easily even if it falls.

strings.重い胴: 外側が重い独楽は、回る勢いがたまって長く回る（はずみ車）: Heavy body: A top with a heavy outside stores spinning energy and spins longer (flywheel).
strings.重さで戻る: 上半身の方が重いと、糸を離した時に自分の重さで元へ戻る。戻る速さは: Returning by weight: If the upper body is heavier, it returns by its own weight when you let go of the string. How fast it returns depends on the weight and on how much the pivot rubs.
strings.重さで戻る: 軸の片側が重いと、離した時に重い方が下がって元の向きへ戻る: Returning by weight: If one side of the pivot is heavy, then when you let go, the heavy side goes down and it returns to its original position.
strings.重さの分け方: 重さが芯の周りに均等だと、回っても芯がぶれない。片寄ると首を振る: How the weight is divided: If the weight is even around the core, the core does not wobble when it spins. If the weight leans to one side, the top wobbles.
strings.重さの置き方: 円盤の外側が重いほど回る勢いがたまり、長く回る（はずみ車と同じ）: Where the weight sits: The heavier the outside of the disc, the more spinning energy it stores, and the longer it spins (the same as a flywheel).
strings.重ねて強くする: 薄い紙でも {0} 枚貼り合わせると曲がりにくい。厚みが曲がり: Stacking to make it strong: Even thin paper is harder to bend when you glue {0} sheet(s) together. The thickness decides how hard it is to bend.
strings.重ねる: 上に重い物を重ねると重心が上がり、倒れやすくなる。釜は風炉より小さいの: Stacking: If you stack a heavy thing on top, the center of gravity goes up, and it tips over more easily. The kettle is smaller than the brazier, so the effect is small.
strings.重ねる: 盃を台に載せるだけの時は、{0} つの重心が縦に並ぶ。ずれると落ちる: Stacking: When you just set the cup on the stand, the {0} centers of gravity line up vertically. If they shift, it falls.

Print a spot at the arm tip for tying the string, and the position marks. Change the order so that you test the weight’s position before closing the body, then glue it (proposal EP-{1}).
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。つる（取っ手）で吊ると、重心が真下に来る向きで止まる: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. When you hang it by the handle, it stops in the position where the center of gravity is right below.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。上が広い形は重心が高く、少しの傾きで台の外へ出やすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. A shape that is wide at the top has a high center of gravity, and a small tilt easily moves it outside the base.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。下がふくらんだ形は重心が低く、押しても戻りやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. A shape that bulges at the bottom has a low center of gravity and comes back easily even if pushed.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。低いほど、傾けても戻りやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. The lower it is, the easier it is for the object to come back after you tilt it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。低いほど、押しても戻りやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. The lower it is, the easier it is for the object to come back when you push it.

strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。台の上にある間は、押しても元へ戻る: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. As long as it is above the base, the object goes back to its original position even if you push it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。底が広く下が重いほど低くなり、倒れにくい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. The wider the bottom and the heavier the lower part, the lower it is, and the harder it is to tip.

strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。背の高い人形ほど重心も高く、少しの傾きで台の外へ出る: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. The taller the doll, the higher the center of gravity, and a small tilt moves it outside the base.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。袋は底に中身がたまるので重心が低く、倒れにくい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. The contents of a bag collect at the bottom, so the center of gravity is low and it is hard to knock over.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。軸より下にあると、傾けた時に戻る向きの力が生まれる: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. When it is below the axis, a force that pulls it back appears when you tilt it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。軸より下に置くと、傾いた時に戻る向きの力が出る: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. If you put it below the axis, a force that pulls it back appears when it tilts.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。首が高く上がった馬は重心が前寄りで、前へ倒れやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object’s weight. A horse with its neck held high has its center of gravity toward the front, and it tips forward easily.
strings.重心: 重さの真ん中が低いほど、揺らしても戻りやすい。下に重りを入れた起き上がり: Center of gravity: The lower the middle of the weight, the more easily it comes back after rocking. This is the idea behind a tumbler toy (okiagari-koboshi) with a weight at the bottom.
strings.重心が低い: 重い所が底にあると、傾けても重心は少ししか上がらず、戻る力が働く: Low center of gravity: If the heavy part is at the bottom, the center of gravity rises only a little when you tilt it, and a force pulls it back.
strings.重心が軸より下: 吊るした物は、重い所が一番下に来る向きで止まる。傾けると戻ろう: Center of gravity below the pivot: A hanging thing settles with its heavy part at the very bottom. If you tilt it, it swings as it tries to come back.
strings.重心と底: 細い首は軽いので重心は低い。底が広いと支える面も広く、戻る力が大きい: Center of gravity and bottom: A thin neck is light, so the center of gravity stays low. If the bottom is wide, the supporting surface is wide too, and the force that brings it back is big.

strings.重心と支える面: 丸くて低い形は重心が低く、支える面も広いので戻りやすい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A round, low shape has a low center of gravity and a wide supporting surface, so it comes back easily.

strings.重心と支える面: 低くて広い形は、傾けても重心が面の外へ出にくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A low, wide shape is less likely to have its center of gravity move outside the surface, even when tilted.

strings.重心と支える面: 台に置く時は、底が広く低いほど倒れにくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: When you set it on a stand, the wider and lower the base, the harder it is to knock over.

strings.重心と支える面: 底が広く屋根が軽いと重心が低い。傾けても戻る: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the bottom is wide and the roof is light, the center of gravity is low. It comes back even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 底が広く背が低いほど、倒れにくい。ふたを重くすると重心が上がる: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the base and the lower the height, the harder it is to knock over. If you make the lid heavy, the center of gravity goes up.
strings.重心と支える面: 底が広く背が低いほど、傾けても倒れにくい。屋根が重いと重心が上: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the base and the lower the height, the harder it is to knock over, even when tilted. If the roof is heavy, the center of gravity goes up and it falls over more easily.
strings.重心と支える面: 底の箱が広く重いと重心が低い。上に伸びる幟は軽いので重心はあま: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the box at the bottom is wide and heavy, the center of gravity is low. The banner reaching upward is light, so the center of gravity does not go up much.
strings.重心と支える面: 座った形は重心が低く、底の面が広い。傾けても重心が面の外へ出に: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A sitting shape has a low center of gravity and a wide bottom surface. The center of gravity is less likely to move outside the surface even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 裾が広いと支える面が広く、傾けても重心が面の外へ出にくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the hem is wide, the supporting surface is wide, and the center of gravity is less likely to move outside the surface even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 裾が広いほど支える面が広く、傾けても戻りやすい。頭が重いと倒れ: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the hem, the wider the supporting surface, and the more easily it comes back when tilted. If the head is heavy, it falls over more easily.
strings.重心と支える面: 足が細く体が高いと重心が高く、少しの傾きで倒れる。台を広げると: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the legs are thin and the body is tall, the center of gravity is high, and it falls over with a small tilt. If you widen the stand, it comes back.
strings.重心と支える面: 重さの真ん中が底の面の真上にある間は、傾けても戻る。はみ出すと: Center of gravity and supporting surface: As long as the middle of the weight is right above the base, it comes back when you tilt it. If it goes past the edge, it falls.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。幅が広く低い形ほど、傾けられる: Center of gravity and supporting surface: While the center of gravity is above the base surface, it comes back. The wider and lower the shape, the bigger the angle you can tilt it.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。幅の広い体は傾けても粘る: Center of gravity and supporting surface: While the center of gravity is above the base surface, it comes back. A wide body hangs on even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。座った形は重心が低く、面が広い: Center of gravity and supporting surface: While the center of gravity is above the base surface, it comes back. A sitting shape has a low center of gravity and a wide surface.

strings.重心と支える面: 開く角度が広いほど、底の面が広がり、少し押しても戻る: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the opening angle, the wider the bottom surface, and it comes back even if you push it a little.
strings.重心と支点: 重心が支点より下にあると、傾けた時に戻る向きの力が働く。上にあると: Center of gravity and pivot: If the center of gravity is below the pivot, a force pushes it back when it tilts. If it is above, it falls over.
strings.重心と軸: あごの重い方が下がって元へ戻るので、糸を離すと口が元の形に戻る: Center of gravity and axle: The heavier side of the jaw goes down and returns, so when you let go of the string, the mouth goes back to its original shape.
strings.重心と軸: 重心が軸より下にあると、傾けた時に戻る力が生まれ、振り子のように揺れ: Center of gravity and axis: When the center of gravity is below the axis, a force that pulls it back appears when you tilt it, and it swings like a pendulum.
strings.重心と軸: 頭の重さの真ん中が軸より下にあると、傾けても元に戻ろうとして揺れる（: Center of gravity and axle: If the middle of the head’s weight is below the axle, it tries to go back when tilted, and it swings (a pendulum).
strings.重心と軸: 顎の重さの真ん中が軸より前にあると、何もしなくても口が開く: Center of gravity and axle: If the middle of the jaw’s weight is in front of the axle, the mouth opens by itself.
strings.重心と軸: 鳥の重さの真ん中が軸より下にあると、傾けても元に戻ろうとして揺れる（: Center of gravity and axle: If the middle of the bird’s weight is below the axle, it tries to go back when tilted, and it swings (a pendulum).
strings.重心のずれ: 片側に長い物を付けると重さの真ん中がその側へ寄る。台をその向きに広: Shifted center of gravity: If you attach something long to one side, the middle of the weight moves toward that side. If you make the stand wider in that direction, it comes back more easily.
